brief.headline: Korean memory whipsaw reverses: SSE/SKH +27%/+30% off AI capex relief rally; HBM4 race tightens as UBS sees Samsung overtaking Hynix in 2027
brief.summary: <cite index="40-8,40-9">SK Hynix closed nearly 30% higher on July 31, marking its best day on record, while Samsung closed nearly 27% higher</cite>, driven by <cite index="42-7">upbeat earnings from Microsoft, Amazon and Meta reinforcing expectations that spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure remains robust</cite>. <cite index="47-5,47-6">UBS projects Samsung to account for 41% of global HBM bit shipments in 2027, narrowly ahead of SK Hynix at 39%, a faster acceleration than its May forecast</cite>. <cite index="16-1,16-2">TrendForce projects DRAM contract prices to rise another 13%-18% in Q3, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 10%-15% QoQ</cite>, extending a multi-quarter rally driven by <cite index="8-3,8-13">full HBM output allocation for the year, with Micron guiding for a 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-long Samsung vs. SK Hynix on 6-12mo view. UBS Aug 2 note marks inflection: Samsung closing HBM4 qual gap faster than Street expected, targeting 41% share in 2027 vs. Hynix 39% (vs. prior parity forecast). Hynix retains 2026 dominance (~50% HBM bits, 57% Q4'25 revenue share per Counterpoint) and superior execution track record, but Samsung's 50% HBM capacity expansion + foundry/logic diversification offers beta on hyperscaler build-out breadth. Near-term, both benefit from record gross margins (MU 68% Q2 guide sets comp) and pricing power intact through 2027. Volatility premium embedded post 10.8% KOSPI single-day drop Jul 29 then 14% reversal Jul 31 creates tactical long entry, but position-sizing discipline critical given 200%+ YTD gains and leverage unwind risk still present in Korean complex.

memory_cycle.notes: HBM-led supercycle diverging from conventional DRAM/NAND. Pricing: Q3 DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ per TrendForce, decelerating from Q2 (DRAM +58-63%, NAND +70-75%) but still triple-digit cumulative gains since Q1'25. Supply: top-3 makers pre-sold 2026 HBM output; hyperscalers locked 2027 LTAs. Demand: $660-690B hyperscaler 2026 capex (Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, MSFT $120B+, Oracle $50B) vs. $600B capex-to-revenue gap widening per Sequoia. Risk: 46% capex/revenue divergence exceeds 2001 telecom (32%), but AI inference transition + CoWoS easing (gap narrowing 20%→10% by end-2026) supports extension into 2027. Consumer DRAM/NAND structurally deprioritized (70% wafer allocation to datacenter per IDC), price resistance emerging in PC/smartphone.

brief.hbm_pulse: HBM4 mass production launched Feb 2026 (both Samsung/Hynix simultaneous). Hynix holds 2026 dominance (48-50% bits, only supplier shipping HBM4 at scale per company guidance), but Samsung closing fast: UBS Aug 2 updated forecast shows Samsung 41% 2027 share vs. Hynix 39%, Micron 20%—ahead of May parity call. Pricing: HBM3E up ~20% for 2026 deliveries (Digitimes Dec'25), minimal-to-modest HBM4 downtick expected vs. 2025 levels per UBS July note. Nvidia secured 60% of 2026 CoWoS capacity (515K wafers TSMC, 80K Amkor/ASE) locking Samsung/Hynix into Rubin/Vera roadmaps. Constraint shifting: CoWoS gap compressing (TSMC 120-140K wafers/mo 2026 vs. 75-80K late'25), but HBM bit demand +35% YoY to 17.1B Gb. Stargate 900K wafer/mo LTA with Samsung/Hynix remains anchor tenant. Watch Samsung HBM4 Nvidia qual timing—any slip extends Hynix pricing power into 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung to overtake SK Hynix in HBM market by 2027, UBS projects
news_pulse.implication: Accelerated Samsung HBM4 ramp narrows Hynix's structural moat; 41% vs. 39% 2027 share split implies margin compression risk for Hynix if Samsung pricing aggressive on qual wins. Positive for Samsung foundry/packaging synergies.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix, Samsung post record single-day gains (+30%, +27%) on AI capex relief rally
news_pulse.implication: Violent reversal after Jul 29 -10.8% KOSPI selloff confirms positioning extremely bearish into MSFT/AMZN earnings. Foreign buying + SK Group Chairman share purchases (disclosed Jul 31) stabilized sentiment. Short-covering + levered ETF rebalancing amplified move—sustainability depends on sustained foreign inflows.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex consensus revised to $660-690B, up 81% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, MSFT $120B+ confirms memory demand floor intact. 75% allocated to AI infrastructure (GPUs, HBM, networking). $600B capex-revenue gap (Sequoia) and 46% divergence (Allianz) above 2001 telecom threshold, but supply-constrained posture (all hyperscalers guided) supports pricing.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Monthly capacity reaching 120-140K wafers (vs. 75-80K late'25) eases GPU assembly bottleneck, removing constraint on HBM attach. Nvidia Rubin/Vera ramps accelerate 2H26. Spillover to OSAT (Amkor 180-190K wafers, SPIL 60-80K annual outsource) diversifies supply but TSMC retains anchor position.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ—rally decelerating but positive
news_pulse.implication: Sequential gains slowing from Q2 (+58-63% DRAM, +70-75% NAND) as consumer affordability caps PC/smartphone ASP pass-through. Server DRAM price moderation tied to hyperscaler LTAs locking rates. AI demand keeps floor under pricing, but peak rate-of-change likely Q2.

news_pulse.headline: Micron guides 68% gross margin in Q2 2026 on HBM mix shift
news_pulse.implication: Sets comp for Samsung/Hynix HBM-heavy product mix. Every HBM wafer is 3-5x revenue vs. DDR5, zero-sum trade-off with consumer. Validates pricing power through 2027, but also highlights consumer margin compression risk if hyperscaler demand plateaus.

news_pulse.headline: Bank of America: 2026 DRAM revenue +51%, NAND +45%, ASPs +30%+
news_pulse.implication: BofA labels 2026 '1990s-style supercycle,' names SK Hynix top pick. Revenue growth driven by volume (AI server DRAM/NAND content doubling per box) + ASP (HBM premium, conventional tightness). Supports thesis memory shortages extend to 2027-28.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix warns memory shortage may persist past 2030 as datacenter consumes 70% output
news_pulse.implication: CEO July guidance extends shortage timeline beyond prior 2027-28 consensus. HBM consuming 23% of total DRAM wafer output in 2026 (up from 19% in 2025) per Fortune, structural reallocation away from consumer. Implies Samsung/Hynix capacity discipline rational, pricing power durable barring demand shock.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely elevated vol premium post ±20% single-session swings Jul 29-31. Korea Exchange briefly halted program buying Jul 31 on +5.1% intraday KOSPI spike (closed +2.3%), indicating circuit-breaker proximity. Implied vol for Samsung/Hynix ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) elevated but mean-reverting from panic levels. Options skew likely normalizing after forced deleveraging cleared. No specific derivatives data in payload, but violent bi-directional moves + margin-call liquidations suggest realized vol >60% annualized for Korean memory complex in July. Short-dated straddles expensive; prefer 3-6mo structures if expressing view.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung HBM4 Nvidia qualification update—any formal announcement accelerates 2027 share gain thesis and pressures Hynix premium
Hyperscaler earnings call transcripts (MSFT/AMZN/META Jul 30-31)—parse memory procurement commentary, LTA terms, capex allocation to GPUs vs. networking/power
KOSPI foreign flow data—Jul 31 rally attributed to foreign buying reversing deleveraging; sustained inflows required to confirm technical bottom vs. dead-cat bounce
TrendForce/DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates—any divergence between contract (+13-18% Q3 guide) and spot would signal demand softness or inventory overhang
CoWoS OSAT capacity announcements—Amkor/ASE expansions beyond 240-270K wafer annual outsource would further ease GPU supply constraints, bullish for HBM attach rates
